questions.title: Day of Week Enumeration
questions.description:
Define an enum Day { SUNDAY, MONDAY, ..., SATURDAY }. Read an integer n in [0, 6] and print the three-letter abbreviation for that day (SUN, MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT). For out-of-range input print INVALID.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: the day abbreviation or INVALID.

Constraints:
-1 <= n <= 10

questions.title: Explicit Priority Enum Values
questions.description:
Define an enum Priority with explicit values: LOW=100, MEDIUM=200, HIGH=300, CRITICAL=400. Read an integer in [1, 4] mapping to LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL respectively. Print the numeric value of the chosen priority. For out-of-range input default to LOW.

Input Format:
A single integer choice (1-4).

Output Format:
A single integer: the priority value.

Constraints:
0 <= choice <= 10

questions.title: Typedef for Distance Units
questions.description:
Use typedef to define Kilometers and Meters as aliases for int. Read a distance in kilometers and print the equivalent in meters (1 km = 1000 m).

Input Format:
A single integer km.

Output Format:
A single integer: the distance in meters.

Constraints:
0 <= km <= 1000

questions.title: Point Struct Manhattan Distance
questions.description:
Define a typedef struct Point with fields x, y. Read a single point and print its Manhattan distance from the origin (|x| + |y|).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
A single integer: |x| + |y|.

Constraints:
-1000 <= x, y <= 1000

questions.title: Status Enum Switch
questions.description:
Define an enum Status { STATUS_OK, STATUS_WARN, STATUS_ERROR }. Read an integer and print the corresponding label: OK, WARN, ERROR. For any other value print UNKNOWN.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: OK, WARN, ERROR, or UNKNOWN.

Constraints:
-1 <= n <= 10

questions.title: IntPtr Typedef Dereference
questions.description:
Define typedef int* IntPtr. Read an integer v, take its address via an IntPtr, and print the value dereferenced from the pointer plus 1.

Input Format:
A single integer v.

Output Format:
A single integer: v + 1.

Constraints:
-1000 <= v <= 1000

questions.title: Traffic Light State Transition
questions.description:
A traffic light cycles RED -> GREEN -> YELLOW -> RED. Define an enum Light { RED, YELLOW, GREEN }. Read the current state (0=RED, 1=YELLOW, 2=GREEN) and print the next state's integer value.

Input Format:
A single integer current state.

Output Format:
A single integer: the next state (0, 1, or 2).

Constraints:
-1 <= state <= 5

questions.title: Playing Card Suit Lookup
questions.description:
A card game uses an enum Suit { HEARTS, DIAMONDS, CLUBS, SPADES }. Read a suit index (0-3) and print its single-letter code (H, D, C, S). For out-of-range input print ?.

Input Format:
A single integer suit index.

Output Format:
A single character code followed by a newline.

Constraints:
-1 <= suit <= 10

questions.title: Quarterly Bonus Payout Reporter
questions.description:
A payroll system stores employees using typedef struct Employee { int id; int salary; }. Read id and salary, compute a 10% bonus, and print id and total (salary + bonus) on one line.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: id and salary.

Output Format:
A single line: id total.

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10000, 0 <= salary <= 100000

questions.title: HTTP Status Code Lookup
questions.description:
An HTTP server uses an enum HttpStatus with explicit values HTTP_OK=200, HTTP_NOT_FOUND=404, HTTP_SERVER_ERROR=500. Read a numeric status code and print "code LABEL" if known (OK, NOT_FOUND, SERVER_ERROR), else print "0 UNKNOWN".

Input Format:
A single integer HTTP status code.

Output Format:
A single line: code LABEL, or 0 UNKNOWN.

Constraints:
0 <= code <= 600

questions.title: Color Brightness via Enum Switch
questions.description:
A graphics module defines enum Color { COLOR_RED=1, COLOR_GREEN=2, COLOR_BLUE=3, COLOR_BLACK=10 }. Read a color code and look up its brightness via a switch on the Color enum (RED=50, GREEN=100, BLUE=75, BLACK=0, default 0). Print the brightness value. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
A single integer color code.

Output Format:
A single integer: brightness.

Constraints:
0 <= code <= 99

questions.title: Point Distance with Typedef Struct
questions.description:
Define typedef struct Point { int x, y; }. Read two points (p1 and p2, each on its own line) and print their Manhattan distance (|p1.x-p2.x| + |p1.y-p2.y|). Do not use pow or sqrt.

Input Format:
Line 1: x1 y1. Line 2: x2 y2.

Output Format:
A single integer: the Manhattan distance.

Constraints:
-1000 <= coordinates <= 1000

questions.title: Function Pointer BinOp Dispatch
questions.description:
Define typedef int (*BinOp)(int, int) and three functions add, sub, mul. Read op (1=add, 2=sub, 3=mul) and two integers a, b. Dispatch via a BinOp variable and print the result. Default op (any other value) acts as add. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers: op a b.

Output Format:
A single integer: the result.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000

questions.title: Permission Flag Enumeration
questions.description:
A file system uses enum Flag { FLAG_A=1<<0, FLAG_B=1<<1, FLAG_C=1<<2, FLAG_D=1<<3 }. Read an integer bitmask n. Build a Flag value by OR'ing in each flag whose bit is set in n. Print the count of flags actually set in the resulting Flag value. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
A single integer n in [0, 15].

Output Format:
A single integer: count of set flags.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 15

questions.title: Matrix Trace via Typedef
questions.description:
Define typedef int Matrix[3][3]. Read 9 integers row-by-row, compute the trace (sum of diagonal m[0][0] + m[1][1] + m[2][2]) and print it. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Three lines of three space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
A single integer: the trace.

Constraints:
-1000 <= matrix values <= 1000

questions.title: Order Status Transition Machine
questions.description:
An e-commerce backend uses enum OrderStatus { ORDER_PENDING, ORDER_PROCESSING, ORDER_SHIPPED, ORDER_DELIVERED, ORDER_CANCELLED }. Read a current status (0-4) and print the next status according to the rules: PENDING->PROCESSING, PROCESSING->SHIPPED, SHIPPED->DELIVERED, DELIVERED->DELIVERED (terminal), CANCELLED->CANCELLED (terminal). Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
A single integer current status (0-4).

Output Format:
A single integer: the next status.

Constraints:
0 <= status <= 4

questions.title: Function Pointer Table Calculator
questions.description:
Implement a calculator using a typedef'd function pointer BinOp and a lookup table ops[5] indexed by opcode (1=add, 2=sub, 3=mul, 4=div with zero-divisor returning 0). Read op a b. For op out of [1,4], print 0. Dispatch via the table and print the result. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers: op a b.

Output Format:
A single integer: the computed result.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000, op in [-1, 10]

questions.title: Inventory Value with Typedef Struct
questions.description:
An inventory system uses enum Category { CAT_ELECTRONICS, CAT_CLOTHING, CAT_FOOD, CAT_BOOKS } and typedef struct Product { int id; int quantity; int unit_price; Category cat; }. Read id, quantity, unit_price, category (0-3). Compute the total value (quantity * unit_price) and print "id value". Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Four space-separated integers: id, quantity, unit_price, category.

Output Format:
A single line: id value.

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10000, 0 <= quantity <= 1000, 0 <= unit_price <= 10000, 0 <= category <= 3

questions.title: Process State Machine via Enum
questions.description:
A process scheduler uses enum State { STATE_IDLE, STATE_ACTIVE, STATE_PAUSED, STATE_STOPPED } and enum Event { EVENT_START, EVENT_PAUSE, EVENT_STOP, EVENT_RESUME }. Read current state s (0-3) and event e (0-3). Compute the next state via transition rules: IDLE+START->ACTIVE; ACTIVE+PAUSE->PAUSED; ACTIVE+STOP->STOPPED; PAUSED+RESUME->ACTIVE; PAUSED+STOP->STOPPED; STOPPED is terminal. Print the next state integer. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: s e.

Output Format:
A single integer: the next state.

Constraints:
0 <= s, e <= 3

questions.title: Callback Handler Dispatch
questions.description:
A GUI framework declares typedef void (*Handler)(int, int*). Define handlers handler_add (adds v to *out), handler_mul (multiplies *out by v), handler_sub (subtracts v from *out). Read op (1=add, 2=mul, 3=sub), accumulator, and value. Dispatch via a Handler and print the final accumulator value. Default op acts as add. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers: op accumulator value.

Output Format:
A single integer: the new accumulator value.

Constraints:
-1000 <= accumulator, value <= 1000
